Verdict: approve.

Approve. eg5 wins on replicated, discriminating evidence rather than any single toxic well: the non-toxic wells at 1 micromolar rep1, 1 micromolar rep2 and 3 micromolar all vote eg5 with sims 4.36e-01 while every stabilizer-leaning phenotype concedes it cannot resolve monopolar spindles for spindle-membrane reasons. budget is exhausted and no further affordable test could overturn the vote. accept eg5 at 0.75 as calibrated given the replicated non-toxic support.

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: the call was **Eg5 inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **Eg5 inhibitors**.

The final call is the nearest-neighbour vote over the 4 wells the agent chose (3/4). The Scientist's own call was **Eg5 inhibitors** (agrees; right).

## Reflection

The call was correct because replicated non-toxic wells carried the decision: 1 µM rep1, 1 µM rep2 and 3 µM with 356-469 cells all nearest-neighbored to Eg5 inhibitors at similarities 0.788, 0.839 and 0.801 for 3/4 votes, with dose-dependent frac_mitotic_like increase rho=+0.95 supporting Eg5-like arrest over random toxicity. I correctly discounted the single discordant 10 µM well with only 28 cells, tub_glcm_contrast z=+203 and frac_mitotic_like z=+159, as a low-cell-count toxic outlier voting Actin disruptors at only 0.52 similarity.

What misled me was the stabilizer-like signal: both microscopist reads favored Microtubule stabilizers and tub_mean rose dose-dependently rho=+0.95 with tub_mean z=+26 to +29, which kept stabilizers at 0.30 then 0.15 in my hypotheses. In retrospect increased tubulin intensity/texture and high act_std z=+30-36 and act_glcm_contrast z=+29-144 reflected rounded mitotics and condensed monopolar spindles rather than true stabilization, and low-resolution fields could not resolve monopolar spindles as noted in review.

Early atlas k-neighbours splitting 6/10 Eg5 vs 4/10 Microtubule destabilizers also slowed convergence, but acquiring the 3 µM neighbour well and 1 µM replicate to test reproducibility resolved the split to 7/10 Eg5 and NSC 3/4 Eg5.

What was right:
- Trusted replicated NSC vote 3/4 Eg5 at high similarity 0.788-0.839 from e9 and protocol tally over e2, e7, e8 rather than single-well call
- Used dose_response frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.95 in e11 as discriminating Eg5 arrest signal consistent with Eg5 inhibitor-induced mitotic arrest (PMID 19351824) and Eg5-mediated mitotic arrest (PMID 28392145)
- Identified 10 µM well w_4c0c203d43 with n=28 cells in e3 as toxic outlier and down-weighted its Actin disruptor vote similarity 0.52
- Acquired intermediate 3 µM well e7 and 1 µM replicate e8 to test reproducibility instead of stopping at initial 1/2 split vote in e5

What was wrong or missed:
- Over-weighted microscopist Microtubule stabilizer calls in e4 and e10 despite conceded inability to resolve monopolar spindles
- Misread tub_mean dose increase rho=+0.95 in e12 and tub_mean z=+26.4 to +29.5 in e2/e7 as stabilizer support rather than condensed monopolar spindle intensity
- Misread very high actin texture signals act_std z=+36.1 and act_glcm_contrast z=+144.1 in e2/e3 as potential Actin disruptor signal rather than secondary rounding of mitotically arrested cells
- Initial hypothesis split Eg5 0.35 / destabilizer 0.30 / stabilizer 0.30 in e6 gave too much weight to k-neighbour destabilizer votes 4/10 from toxic well in e5

Proposed next experiment: High-resolution immunofluorescence for alpha-tubulin plus DNA / phospho-histone H3 in the 1-3 µM range to score monopolar rosette spindles and mitotic index versus a reference Eg5 inhibitor and a microtubule stabilizer control.

Citations verified: 4/4

- PMID [19351824](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19351824/): K858, a novel inhibitor of mitotic kinesin Eg5 and antitumor agent, induces cell death in cancer cells. *Cancer Res* (2009) — Eg5 inhibition induces mitotic arrest and cell death in cancer cells.
- PMID [28392145](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28392145/): HDAC Inhibitor-Induced Mitotic Arrest Is Mediated by Eg5/KIF11 Acetylation. *Cell Chem Biol* (2017) — Eg5/KIF11 acetylation mediates mitotic arrest.
- PMID [34958711](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34958711/): Optical Control of Mitosis with a Photoswitchable Eg5 Inhibitor. *Angew Chem Int Ed Engl* (2022) — Direct Eg5 inhibition controls mitosis and spindle morphology.
